title: Carpal bones and metacarpals (palmar)
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender; surface detail added with an image model.

rows: Most lateral bone of the proximal row of the carpus, in the floor of the anatomical snuffbox.
Radius, lunate, capitate, trapezium, and trapezoid.
hy: The most often fractured carpal bone, typically after a fall on an outstretched hand, with tenderness in the anatomical snuffbox. Its blood supply enters distally, so the proximal part is at risk of avascular necrosis.

So Long To Pinky, Here Comes The Thumb: the proximal row from lateral to medial (Scaphoid, Lunate, Triquetrum, Pisiform), then the distal row from medial to lateral (Hamate, Capitate, Trapezoid, Trapezium).

rows: Proximal row of the carpus, between the scaphoid and the triquetrum.
Radius, scaphoid, triquetrum, capitate, and hamate.
hy: The most often dislocated carpal bone. A lunate displaced toward the palm can compress the median nerve in the carpal tunnel.

rows: Medial side of the proximal row of the carpus. The pisiform sits on its palmar surface.
Lunate, pisiform, hamate, and the articular disc of the distal radioulnar joint.
Pea-shaped sesamoid bone in the tendon of flexor carpi ulnaris, on the palmar surface of the triquetrum.
Most lateral bone of the distal row of the carpus, at the base of the thumb.
Scaphoid, trapezoid, and the 1st and 2nd metacarpals. Its joint with the 1st metacarpal is a saddle joint, which gives the thumb its wide range of movement.
Distal row of the carpus, between the trapezium and the capitate.
Scaphoid, trapezium, capitate, and the 2nd metacarpal.
Center of the distal row of the carpus. It is the largest carpal bone.
Scaphoid, lunate, trapezoid, hamate, and the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th metacarpals (mainly the 3rd).
Most medial bone of the distal row of the carpus. Its hook projects toward the palm.
Lunate, triquetrum, capitate, and the 4th and 5th metacarpals.
hy: A fracture of the hook of the hamate can injure the ulnar nerve in the ulnar (Guyon) canal, which runs between the hook and the pisiform.

rows: Bone of the thumb within the palm. It is the shortest and most mobile metacarpal.
Trapezium, at a saddle joint, and the proximal phalanx of the thumb.
Bone of the palm leading to the index finger. It is the longest metacarpal.
Trapezoid mainly, also the trapezium and capitate; the 3rd metacarpal; and the proximal phalanx of the index finger.
Bone of the palm leading to the middle finger.
Capitate; the 2nd and 4th metacarpals; and the proximal phalanx of the middle finger.
Bone of the palm leading to the ring finger.
Capitate and hamate; the 3rd and 5th metacarpals; and the proximal phalanx of the ring finger.
Bone of the palm leading to the little finger.
Hamate; the 4th metacarpal; and the proximal phalanx of the little finger.
hy: Boxer's fracture: a fracture of the neck of the 5th metacarpal from punching with a closed fist.
